engineers: PHMSA found that the LNG trapped in the 18-inch VIP warmed and boiled for about five days (closed at 16:44 on 3 June 2022) and raised the pressure from 37 psig to 1,313 psig, rupturing the pipe at 11:28 on 8 June 2022: about 10,000 lb of methane released in roughly 9 seconds, a BLEVE and a fireball about 450 ft high. Causes cited: the segment's pressure safety valve was isolated for its annual test on 26 April 2022 and never restored; the transfer procedure did not specify the two valve positions, so the operator unknowingly blocked in an LNG-filled segment; and the inner-pipe skin temperature points were logged but not alarmed, so the warming was not noticed.
source: PHMSA, Amended Notice of Probable Violation CPF 4-2024-033-NOPV, 20 December 2024, pp.1-4
note: Withheld from the agent: basis.md stops at the second valve closure and contains no pressure after it.
